changes: Runtime package only: on a Modwerk base that owns 0x40004100 and 0x40006820 (sdk/machines/octatrack/events.json), POLY8 subscribes instead of patching them: ev_play_increment (order 20) takes POLY tracks, ev_voice_bind (order 20) handles resets its renderer causes, ev_voice_bind_run discards a track's extension voices when a reset runs. Repitch and Mute Modes then install beside it without POLY8 linking their code.
The subscribers are appended to polyphony.s under MODWERK_EVENTS with absolute addressing, so no existing PC-relative displacement moves; native octabam builds assemble byte-identical.

Limits: needs a base built with site events; older bases refuse this package, and Undo keeps 0.2.7-experimental for them. Emulator evidence only (synthetic renderer flags and register state); current-build hardware, chip worst-case timing and complete memory bounds remain unqualified.

USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB as one independent package beside every other module, on a Modwerk base built with site events. What it shares with other machines goes through the base's machine chooser table and take events instead of a machine group, and its authored bytes that coincide with stock are rebuilt from your own OS at install. Emulator and host tests only; no hardware run of this package. The owner waived hardware evidence for this exact version's USB package for the beta.
Media-only: replace the POLY8 thumbnail with an original eight-voice sample diagram using the library’s shared grid, lavender signal palette and typography.

Release the previous sequenced chord once before the next native sample trig, so finite AMP REL can end its tails even with HOLD INF. Preserve all notes in the new chord and independently owned panel/MIDI notes. Related to https://github.com/repeat98/modwerk/issues/447.
Keep finite HOLD, intentional REL INF sustain and native STOP behavior. Recorded key-up timing remains unsupported; the final chord with HOLD INF sustains until another trig or STOP.

The owner approved this scoped experimental release with current-build hardware, chip worst-case timing and complete memory qualification waived. Native playback tests pass; physical MKI confirmation remains pending. Keep issue 447 open until the exact published download is verified on the affected unit.
Combine POLY8 with Repitch, Mute Modes and Scale Quantizer through guarded shared hooks; other configurations retain their original build paths.
Add a bounded native chooser for POLY8, Analog BD, VECTOR and FM Synth together. Each machine retains its own saved Part marker, controls and playback engine.
Use FM Synth’s bundled signature-aware quantizer when both quantizers are selected; preserve its complete helper-pointer ABI and refuse changed or unknown overlapping claims.

Keep the pitch cache within signed ColdFire PC-relative addressing range; prevent silent assembler displacement wrap from overwriting preceding companion-machine code. Add a firmware-free check of all 121 compiled local PC-relative addresses.
Restore NO dismissal of the one-POLY8 refusal using stock’s modal input layer while retaining its automatic native timeout.
Retain eight POLY8 voices, one POLY8 assignment per Part, LOOP OFF on new assignments and fixed 1/8 gain. Existing DSP memory and menu-space limits still apply; Octakit remains incompatible.

Load the shared chooser initialization flag explicitly instead of relying on uncleared BSS. Nonzero RAM reproduces an odd widget target at the T07/T08 boot-failure call; add a compiled-section startup-state gate. T07/T08 are withdrawn; the owner reports corrected T09 works on MKII, without a separate test checklist.

The owner reports exact T10 “works like a charm” on MKII and approves this scoped experimental release. Separately reported recording/load/persistence cases, chip worst-case timing and complete memory bounds remain unverified; combined-machine results are emulator evidence.

Preserve current VECTOR 0.2.4 packed-setting validation through the shared machine bridge; a sanitizer regression covers all 256 mixed AB/FM/VECTOR signature masks. The exact T10 selection flow is checked against stock FLEX/STATIC controls and the earlier T09 regression.
Match FLEX/STATIC selection: POLY8 assignment and reselection stay on the current page. Double-TRACK opens FLEX samples; LEFT/RIGHT and sample confirmation remain available.
Publish as POLY8, including the machine chooser and refusal dialog, while preserving PL/1 saved-Part identity.
First public experimental release: eight shared sample voices, one POLY per Part, independent envelopes and fixed 1/8 gain.
POLY8T06 preserves an existing POLY track’s LOOP setting when reselecting the machine; newly assigned tracks still default to OFF.
Returning LEFT from POLY’s sample slots restores the POLY machine cursor and title; RIGHT opens FLEX samples again.

Reduce ColdFire interpolation and held-voice mixing instructions without changing eight-voice admission, envelopes or fixed 1/8 gain. Skip redundant peak measurement while the limiter is at unity, retaining defensive output saturation.
Retain the original DSP payloads and existing core logger. Native load comparisons and panel flows are emulator evidence; physical CPU deadlines, recording and reboot qualification remain pending.
Panel recording supports at most four notes spanning eleven semitones; recorded duration follows AMP HOLD. Extended MIDI recording and grid root editing remain incomplete.

POLY8T05 private test preserves both original 1.40C DSP uploads byte for byte and bypasses the SDK automatic stock-effect dynamic loader. The build refuses DSP drift or an implicit loader. This isolates a dependency candidate after T04 hardware logs showed no sample-render entries; it is not a confirmed hardware fix.
Add bounded counts for native command-consumer and AMP-builder calls, including stock tracks. The existing core logger snapshots them outside audio callbacks.

Retain eight voices, one POLY per Part, fixed 1/8 gain, LOOP OFF for new assignments, scratch bounds, timed modal and marker persistence correction. Physical recording, reboot and transport/audio results remain unverified on this version.

POLY8T04 private diagnostic candidate includes the existing core OCTAMOD.LOG logger and bounded once-per-second POLY transport, render/fetch, key/record, voice and modal snapshots. No filesystem work occurs in audio or UI callbacks.

Reserve scratch buffers for all 32 physical selectors while retaining the eight-active-voice cap; sparse extension indices can no longer address beyond scratch storage. This is a defensive bounds correction, not a confirmed cause of the MKII stall.
Keep the one-POLY refusal modal but automatically dismiss it after 120 native UI ticks, so an overlooked dialog cannot indefinitely capture panel input.
Retain fixed 1/8 gain, LOOP OFF for new assignments and the battery-RAM marker copy correction. MKII recording and transport/audio failures remain open until this exact build is tested on hardware.
Retain the eight-head cap and pitch-work budget; allow one POLY assignment per Part. Refuse a second machine before any settings/sample writes, with a native NO-dismissed modal.
Apply fixed 1/8 (-18.06 dB) gain in both the single-voice fast path and envelope-weighted mix; leave headroom for eight coherent full-scale voices without voice-count pumping.
Correct the PL/1 marker copy into battery RAM by staging its reads before writes; normal restart can retain POLY identity.

Fresh-assignment native REC+PLAY succeeds, but the previous image also succeeds in that emulator path. The reported MKII recording failure remains unresolved on hardware; do not claim this gain/persistence update fixes it. LOOP OFF default remains unchanged.
Restore the native panel recorder for up to four-note chords spanning eleven semitones; consume encoded roots before normal PTCH locks, retaining native SAMPLE locks.
Limit this hardware test to eight shared voices with pitch-weighted admission; steal released tails before held notes and ignore duplicate held-key presses.
New POLY assignments default to LOOP OFF. Browser confirmations and existing saved LOOP choices retain their value.
Recorded duration follows AMP HOLD; wider chords, extended MIDI recording, grid root editing and physical MKII deadlines remain unqualified.
32 active POLY voices share one global pool; one track can use all free voices.
Independent preallocated AMP envelopes with shared per-track filters and FX.
PTCH tuning is independent of chromatic and MIDI notes, with ten panel octave positions and dedicated-route MIDI 0–127.
Selecting POLY opens native FLEX samples directly; STATIC is excluded.
Hardware deadlines, broad lifecycle combinations, note recording and public packaging remain unqualified.
